title: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
gist: The NYT and other newspaper publishers sued Brave Software, alleging its paywall blocker and search API supply paywalled news to users and AI firms including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere. The suit adds to the NYT's actions against Perplexity and OpenAI/Microsoft.

insights.claim: The NYT and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software in SDNY, alleging it bypasses paywalls and sells the content to AI companies, naming Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere as customers.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Legal risk is extending from AI model developers to the data infrastructure suppliers feeding them.
insights.quote: “Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content

insights.claim: The suit claims Brave made more than $100 million from copying and rereselling publisher work, citing third-party revenue estimates, while publishers received nothing.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Gives a damages and valuation reference for the search-index-as-AI-feed business.
insights.quote: “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,”

insights.claim: The suit says AI companies pay Brave for real-time content from its search index, used both to train models and to answer user queries, and points to Brave's marketing that its Search API is used by Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Search APIs are a growing channel for AI firms to obtain current content, now exposed to copyright claims.

insights.claim: The NYT alleges direct, contributory and vicarious copyright infringement plus DMCA circumvention of technological access controls, and seeks an injunction, statutory and actual damages, and disgorgement of Brave's ad-substitution profits.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Broad remedies sought, including disgorgement, raise potential liability for intermediaries.

insights.claim: Brave's browser has a paywall blocker that is enabled by default and can be turned off; the author found it allowed reading a paywalled NYT article, and Brave's ad blocking replaces ads with its own, offering users a share of the revenue.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The default-on setting is a key fact in claims of deliberate inducement.
insights.quote: “The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,”

insights.claim: The New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel companies filed a similar suit, with their lawyer arguing that AI firms use Brave as a back door and that buying stolen goods secondhand doesn't make them legitimate.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Publishers are coordinating on a supply-chain theory of liability.

insights.claim: The NYT sued Perplexity in December 2025 alleging verbatim or near-verbatim outputs, and Perplexity responded by calling the NYT's claims disinformation without identifying specific inaccuracies.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Perplexity's defense hinges on whether fetching in response to user queries is 'volitional conduct'.

insights.claim: The NYT's December 2023 suit against OpenAI and Microsoft is heading toward trial, with OpenAI arguing its use of news articles is fair use.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A fair-use ruling at trial would set the key precedent for AI training data costs.
